plates.side_label: 8 FRUIT-FLY HOX GENES VS 39 HUMAN HOX GENES (4 CLUSTERS): 180-BP HOMEOBOX (60-AA HOMEODOMAIN) IN HEAD-TO-TAIL COLINEAR ORDER
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Hox Gene Colinearity & Embryonic Body-Plan chart from Spemann & Mangold (1924 Arch. Mikr. Anat. Entw. 100: 599–638), Lewis (7 December 1978 Nature 276: 565–570), Nüsslein-Volhard & Wieschaus (30 October 1980 Nature 287: 795–801), and Scott & Weiner / McGinnis, Levine, Hafen, Kuroiwa & Gehring (March–July 1984 Nature 308: 428–433 & PNAS 81: 4115–4119) aligns the 8 Drosophila Hox genes along chromosome 3 with the 39 human HOX genes across 4 clusters (HOXA, HOXB, HOXC, HOXD), showing 3'-to-5' chromosomal order matching anterior-to-posterior (head-to-tail) expression driven by the conserved 180-bp homeobox (60-amino-acid homeodomain).

teach_overlay.label: COLINEAR HOX ARCHITECT GENES: 8 FLY HOX GENES ↔ 39 HUMAN HOX GENES (4 CLUSTERS) SHARING THE 180-BP HOMEOBOX IN HEAD-TO-TAIL ORDER
teach_overlay.detail: Inked chromosomal colinearity chart on period paper comparing the 8 fruit-fly homeotic genes (lab, pb, Dfd, Scr, Antp, Ubx, abd-A, Abd-B) and the 39 mammalian/human HOX genes (4 clusters), all sharing the conserved 180-base-pair homeobox (60-amino-acid DNA-binding homeodomain) and arranged along the chromosome in the exact head-to-tail order of the body segments they build
teach_overlay.scale: your body's master architect genes are lined up along your chromosome like stations on a railway line — the genes at the front of the DNA strand build your head and neck, the middle genes build your chest and ribs, and the genes at the end build your lower back and limbs

plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period parchment, an inked Spemann-Mangold Dorsal Blastopore Lip Transplant diagram (from Spemann & Mangold 1924 Arch. Mikr. Anat. Entw. 100: 599–638, embryo 1921 Um 132) shows a tiny unpigmented graft from Triton cristatus transplanted onto the ventral flank of a dark Triton taeniatus host embryo, inducing >80% dark host belly cells to fold into a complete secondary neural tube, notochord, somites, and twin head.

teach_overlay.label: MAY 1921 SPEMANN & MANGOLD ORGANIZER (EMBRYO UM 132): PALE DORSAL LIP GRAFT RECRUITS >80% DARK HOST BELLY CELLS INTO TWIN SPINE
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Spemann-Mangold (May 1921 / 1924 Arch. Mikr. Anat. Entw. 100: 599–638) chimera cross-section showing unpigmented donor organizer cells (dorsal blastopore lip) recruiting >80% pigmented host ventral ectoderm cells into a secondary brain and spinal cord
teach_overlay.scale: transplanting a speck of organizer tissue smaller than a pinhead onto an embryo's belly is like dropping a conductor onto a building site — it orders the surrounding skin cells to stop making belly skin and build a second brain and spine instead
